es: Reconocer en un ensayo breve la tesis, las frases temáticas y la conclusión, y saber qué función cumple cada parte.

teaching.en: A strong introduction hooks the reader and ends with a thesis statement, the sentence that tells us exactly what the essay will defend.
teaching.es: Una buena introducción engancha al lector y termina con un enunciado de tesis, la frase que dice exactamente qué defenderá el ensayo.
teaching.explanationEs: La tesis suele ocupar la última frase de la introducción.
segments: A strong introduction hooks the reader and ends with a thesis statement,
the sentence that tells us exactly what the essay will defend.
teaching.audioText: A strong introduction hooks the reader and ends with a thesis statement, the sentence that tells us exactly what the essay will defend.

teaching.en: Each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence, so a reader who skims only first lines still sees what the essay argues.
teaching.es: Cada párrafo de desarrollo abre con una frase temática, así que un lector que solo ojea las primeras líneas ve igualmente lo que el ensayo sostiene.
teaching.explanationEs: Argues que + oración: el ensayo toma una postura.
segments: Each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence, so a reader
who skims only first lines still sees what the essay argues.
teaching.audioText: Each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence, so a reader who skims only first lines still sees what the essay argues.

teaching.en: The rest of the paragraph supports that opening claim with evidence, examples and reasons, each one linked to the point above.
teaching.es: El resto del párrafo respalda esa afirmación inicial con pruebas, ejemplos y razones, cada una enlazada con el punto anterior.
teaching.explanationEs: Support (verbo) = dar pruebas o razones a favor de una idea.
segments: The rest of the paragraph supports that opening claim with evidence,
examples and reasons, each one linked to the point above.
teaching.audioText: The rest of the paragraph supports that opening claim with evidence, examples and reasons, each one linked to the point above.

teaching.en: Good writers signpost their structure with phrases such as in the first place or by contrast, so readers never lose the thread.
teaching.es: Los buenos autores señalizan su estructura con expresiones como «en primer lugar» o «por el contrario», y así los lectores nunca pierden el hilo.
teaching.explanationEs: Signpost funciona como verbo: marca el camino al lector.
segments: Good writers signpost their structure with phrases such as in the
first place or by contrast, so readers never lose the thread.
teaching.audioText: Good writers signpost their structure with phrases such as in the first place or by contrast, so readers never lose the thread.

teaching.en: A forceful conclusion restates the thesis in fresh words and can round off the essay without introducing a new argument.
teaching.es: Una conclusión contundente reformula la tesis con palabras nuevas y puede cerrar el ensayo sin introducir un argumento nuevo.
teaching.explanationEs: Restates = dice lo mismo con otras palabras; round off = cerrar de forma redonda.
segments: A forceful conclusion restates the thesis in fresh words and
can round off the essay without introducing a new argument.
teaching.audioText: A forceful conclusion restates the thesis in fresh words and can round off the essay without introducing a new argument.

teaching.en: Before writing, draw up an outline to build a case for one position, because a plan shows at once which point is missing.
teaching.es: Antes de escribir, elabora un esquema para argumentar a favor de una postura, porque un plan muestra enseguida qué punto falta.
teaching.explanationEs: Build a case for + sustantivo: construir los argumentos de una postura.
segments: Before writing, draw up an outline to build a case for one
position, because a plan shows at once which point is missing.
teaching.audioText: Before writing, draw up an outline to build a case for one position, because a plan shows at once which point is missing.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la frase temática de este párrafo?

choices.text: Pupils who grow vegetables often try new foods at lunch.
School gardens teach pupils to care for living things.
Gardens also bring neighbours into the school.

feedback.es: La frase temática anuncia la idea del párrafo; las demás la apoyan con un dato y con una consecuencia.

hint.es: Es la frase que abre el párrafo y resume su idea.

origin.text: School gardens teach pupils to care for living things. Pupils who grow vegetables often try new foods at lunch, and teachers report calmer lessons after garden sessions. Gardens also bring neighbours into the school.

prompt.es: Completa: «La introducción termina con un enunciado de tesis.»

answer.text: statement

feedback.es: Thesis statement es el término para la frase que fija la postura del ensayo, normalmente al final de la introducción.

origin.text: A good introduction presents the subject. It ends with a thesis ___ that tells readers exactly what the essay will defend.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cada párrafo de desarrollo abre con una frase temática.»

answer.text: Each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence

feedback.es: Body paragraph es el sujeto; opens with a topic sentence describe cómo empieza.

hint.es: El sujeto es Each body paragraph.

prompt.es: ¿Qué hace la segunda frase respecto a la primera del párrafo?

choices.text: It restates the claim in new words without adding anything.
It backs up the opening claim with an example and a figure.
It brings in a counterargument that the writer will answer later.
It signals that the paragraph is moving on to a new topic.

feedback.es: La segunda frase aporta un ejemplo concreto y una cifra de una encuesta: respalda la afirmación inicial.

origin.text: Uniforms save families money. A typical family spends less on school clothes when one uniform replaces many different clothes, and the school's own survey found that eight in ten parents agreed. Uniforms also reduce arguments about what to wear.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la profesora lee solo las primeras frases.

choices.text: To save time, because examples are rarely important in an essay.
To reach the conclusion before she reads the thesis.
To test whether the topic sentences form a clear outline.
To check that every paragraph begins with a signpost.

feedback.es: Las primeras frases de cada párrafo, leídas juntas, muestran si el esquema del ensayo es claro.

origin.audio: When I read a student essay, I start with the last sentence of the introduction, because that is where the thesis usually sits. Then I read only the first sentence of each body paragraph. If those sentences, put together, tell a clear story, the outline is sound. If they jump from idea to idea, I already know where the essay needs work, before I have read a single example.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la parte del ensayo a la que pertenece.

pairs: Many schools now face a difficult choice.
I will argue that homework should be shorter.
Second, short tasks help pupils to sleep.
To sum up, less homework means better learning.

feedback.es: Cada frase ocupa un lugar distinto: apertura, tesis, frase temática y conclusión.

pairs: Many schools now face a difficult choice.
I will argue that homework should be shorter.
Second, short tasks help pupils to sleep.
To sum up, less homework means better learning.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase del ensayo contiene la tesis?

choices.text: Heat, dust and noise are common problems in towns.
Summer temperatures fell by two degrees in three towns.
Hesitant towns are choosing the problem over the solution.
Every town should plant more trees along its streets.

feedback.es: La tesis es la postura que defiende todo el ensayo y se anuncia con «I will argue that»; las demás frases describen el contexto, aportan datos o cierran.

origin.text: Many towns now struggle with heat, dust and constant noise. I will argue that every town should plant more trees along its streets. First, trees make the air in the streets far cooler. Measurements in three towns show that summer temperatures fell by two degrees where trees were planted. Second, a shaded street is better for trade. Shops on tree-lined streets reported more customers, because people stopped to look at the windows. To sum up, the evidence suggests that streets with trees are cooler, quieter and busier. Towns that hesitate are choosing the problem over the solution.

prompt.es: Escucha el párrafo final y elige qué hace el autor con el coste de abrir por la noche.

choices.text: He concedes the objection, but argues that the evidence still favours his thesis.
He uses the cost to show that his own thesis is unrealistic.
He offers the cost as one more reason to open libraries at night.
He accepts that only a few branches matter, so he gives up his thesis.

feedback.es: El autor admite que abrir de noche cuesta dinero («Of course…»), pero sostiene que las pruebas de los proyectos piloto siguen respaldando su tesis; no la abandona ni usa el coste como argumento a favor.

origin.audio: The final paragraph of the essay reads like this. Libraries that close at six serve only those who finish work early, and the readers who need them most are left outside. Of course, opening at night costs money, and I do not claim that every branch must do it. But the pilot schemes leave little room for doubt: where doors stayed open, membership rose by a third. Councils that refuse to look at those figures are defending a timetable, not their readers.

prompt.es: Completa: «En el último párrafo el autor retoma la tesis con otras palabras.»

answer.text: restates

feedback.es: Una buena conclusión restates la tesis: dice lo mismo con otras palabras y sin añadir ideas nuevas.

origin.text: The essay ends with a short paragraph. In it, the writer ___ the thesis in fresh words instead of copying it from the introduction.

prompt.es: Escribe la frase de tesis de un ensayo sobre el horario de los colegios.

answer.text: I will argue that schools should start later, because teenagers learn better when they have slept enough.
accepted: I will argue that schools should start later, because teenagers learn better when they have slept enough.
This essay argues that schools should begin later in the morning, since tired pupils cannot learn properly.
I will argue that school should start later, as teenagers concentrate better after a full night of sleep.

feedback.es: Una tesis clara combina una fórmula de postura, la idea que se defiende y una razón breve.

origin.text: Tema: los colegios deberían empezar más tarde. Escribe una frase de tesis con una fórmula como I will argue that… y una razón.

evidenceGroups: schools should start later in the morning

prompt.es: ¿Qué cabe esperar del resto del ensayo a partir de esta introducción?

choices.text: A detailed attack on professional players and their salaries.
A description of sport in general, with no position to defend.
A strong case against watching sport on television.
A comparison of how much famous and ordinary players train.

feedback.es: «I am going to talk about sport» anuncia un tema, no una postura: sin tesis, lo esperable es un texto descriptivo que no defiende nada.

origin.text: Sport is important in modern life. Many people play it and many more watch it on television. Some players earn millions, while others train in the rain for nothing. In this essay I am going to talk about sport.

prompt.es: Completa: «El autor quiere argumentar a favor de horarios más tardíos.»

answer.text: build

feedback.es: Build a case for describe reunir razones y pruebas en favor de una postura.

origin.text: The writer wants to ___ a case for later school hours, so every paragraph supports a single position.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Un esquema muestra de un vistazo qué punto falta.»

answer.text: An outline shows at a glance which point is missing
accepted: An outline shows at a glance which point is missing
At a glance an outline shows which point is missing

feedback.es: Which point is missing es una pregunta indirecta: el verbo va después del sujeto.

es: Enlazar frases sin repetir palabras con this/such, the former/the latter, the same y respectively, y señalar hacia atrás y hacia delante.

teaching.en: Shop owners and residents asked for parking and quiet respectively, so the former wanted access and the latter wanted peace.
teaching.es: Los comerciantes y los vecinos pidieron estacionamiento y tranquilidad respectivamente, así que los primeros querían acceso y los segundos paz.
teaching.explanationEs: Respectively empareja dos listas en el mismo orden; the former y the latter distinguen dos elementos.
segments: Shop owners and residents asked for parking and quiet respectively,
so the former wanted access and the latter wanted peace.
teaching.audioText: Shop owners and residents asked for parking and quiet respectively, so the former wanted access and the latter wanted peace.

teaching.en: The council introduced a ban on cars; such a decision was unpopular at first, yet the aforementioned ban has since reduced noise.
teaching.es: El municipio introdujo una prohibición de autos; una decisión así fue impopular al principio, pero la mencionada prohibición ha reducido el ruido.
teaching.explanationEs: Such a + sustantivo resume y califica la idea anterior; aforementioned es formal.
segments: The council introduced a ban on cars; such a decision was
unpopular at first, yet the aforementioned ban has since reduced noise.
teaching.audioText: The council introduced a ban on cars; such a decision was unpopular at first, yet the aforementioned ban has since reduced noise.

teaching.en: The writer cut the report to one page, thereby saving her readers time, and in doing so she kept her argument clear.
teaching.es: La autora redujo el informe a una página, con lo cual ahorró tiempo a sus lectores, y al hacerlo mantuvo claro su argumento.
teaching.explanationEs: Thereby + gerundio añade el resultado; in doing so retoma la acción anterior.
segments: The writer cut the report to one page, thereby saving her
readers time, and in doing so she kept her argument clear.
teaching.audioText: The writer cut the report to one page, thereby saving her readers time, and in doing so she kept her argument clear.

teaching.en: The buses were late on Monday and Tuesday by ten and twenty minutes respectively, and the same applies to the trams.
teaching.es: Los autobuses llegaron tarde el lunes y el martes con diez y veinte minutos respectivamente, y lo mismo se aplica a los tranvías.
teaching.explanationEs: The same applies to + sustantivo evita repetir toda la frase.
segments: The buses were late on Monday and Tuesday by ten and
twenty minutes respectively, and the same applies to the trams.
teaching.audioText: The buses were late on Monday and Tuesday by ten and twenty minutes respectively, and the same applies to the trams.

teaching.en: The previous paragraph named two causes; the following points explain them, thereby guiding readers backwards and then forwards.
teaching.es: El párrafo anterior nombraba dos causas; los puntos siguientes las explican, con lo cual guían al lector hacia atrás y luego hacia delante.
teaching.explanationEs: Previous mira hacia atrás; following mira hacia delante.
segments: The previous paragraph named two causes; the following points
explain them, thereby guiding readers backwards and then forwards.
teaching.audioText: The previous paragraph named two causes; the following points explain them, thereby guiding readers backwards and then forwards.

teaching.en: Pupils should respect teachers; by the same token, teachers should respect pupils, and in this respect the aforementioned rules are fair.
teaching.es: Los alumnos deben respetar a los profesores; por la misma razón, los profesores deben respetar a los alumnos, y en este sentido las normas mencionadas son justas.
teaching.explanationEs: By the same token introduce un paralelo; in this respect limita el comentario a un aspecto.
segments: Pupils should respect teachers; by the same token, teachers should respect
pupils, and in this respect the aforementioned rules are fair.
teaching.audioText: Pupils should respect teachers; by the same token, teachers should respect pupils, and in this respect the aforementioned rules are fair.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión evita la repetición con una referencia correcta?

choices.text: The council closed the market square. The former upset the traders.
The council closed the market square. Respectively upset the traders.
The council closed the market square. Such a decision upset the traders.

feedback.es: Such a decision resume la acción anterior y la califica; the former exige dos elementos previos y respectively exige dos listas.

hint.es: Busca la referencia que resume la idea anterior en una frase nominal.

origin.text: Original: The council closed the market square. The council's closure of the market square upset the traders.

prompt.es: Completa: «El primero contamina el aire, mientras que el segundo no.»

answer.text: latter

feedback.es: The latter se refiere al segundo de dos elementos ya citados; aquí, los tranvías.

hint.es: Se refiere al segundo de dos elementos.

origin.text: Cars and trams both serve the centre. The former pollutes the air, whereas the ___ does not.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Se cancelaron las clases, y lo mismo se aplica al deporte.»

answer.text: Lessons were cancelled and the same applies to sport

feedback.es: The same applies to + sustantivo extiende lo dicho a otro elemento sin repetirlo.

hint.es: El verbo applies va con to.

prompt.es: ¿Quién dirigió el taller de fotografía?

choices.text: Sara, the former of the two.
Sara and Tom together, since they shared both workshops.
Tom, the latter of the two.
Nobody, because the latter was too nervous to teach.

feedback.es: Respectively empareja música con Sara y fotografía con Tom; Tom es «the latter», el segundo nombrado.

origin.text: Sara and Tom were asked to lead the two workshops, on music and on photography respectively. The former was shy, and the latter, who had never taught before, was nervous. Such a choice might seem odd, but both did well.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué el compromiso agradó a los padres.

choices.text: It was cheaper than either of the original plans.
It allowed them to spend a week in the mountains.
It proved that both children had grown up.
It spared them a long argument between their children.

feedback.es: Los padres temían una larga discusión; el compromiso se la ahorró. El texto no habla de dinero ni de madurez.

origin.audio: My brother and I argued about two holiday plans, a week by the sea and a week in the mountains. The former was my choice and the latter was his. In the end, we chose neither, but such a compromise pleased our parents, who had feared a long argument. The following summer we did the same, and this time nobody complained.

pairs: The former pollute the air.

pairs.es: Se refiere al primero de dos citados

pairs: Such a decision is rarely popular.

pairs.es: Resume y califica la idea anterior

pairs: The following sections explain them.

feedback.es: Cada referencia cumple una función distinta: emparejar, distinguir, resumir y anunciar.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué reprocha la locutora a la autora sobre las dos explicaciones.

choices.text: Favouring the explanation she can measure over one she cannot.
Overlooking that the supermarket opened too late to affect sales.
Ignoring the weather data that the report itself supplies.
Blaming the weather when the supermarket was the real cause.

feedback.es: La autora prefiere la explicación que puede medir («the former»), aunque sea discutible; además omite un tercer factor que aparece en su propia última página.

origin.audio: The report gives two explanations for the fall in sales, the new supermarket and the bad weather. The former is easy to measure, since the supermarket opened in March; the latter is not, because weather data for the region is incomplete. The author nonetheless blames the supermarket, and in doing so she gives more weight to the evidence she happens to have. Such a choice is understandable, but it is open to question. By the same token, the report ignores the third factor mentioned on its own last page, the rise in fuel prices, which may well account for a good part of the drop.

prompt.es: ¿Qué reescritura elimina la repetición sin crear ambigüedad?

choices.text: The report names two causes. It began on Monday and on Wednesday, and it was short and heavy, as the report itself says in this respect.
The report names two causes, the strike and the snow; the former began on Monday and the latter on Wednesday, short and heavy respectively.
The report names two causes, the strike and the snow; the latter began on Monday and the former on Wednesday, short and heavy respectively.
The report names two causes, the strike and the snow; both began on Monday, short and heavy respectively.

feedback.es: Solo la versión con the former, the latter y respectively en el orden correcto mantiene la correspondencia (huelga-lunes-corta, nieve-miércoles-intensa).

origin.text: Original: The report names two causes of the delay, the strike and the snow. The strike began on Monday, and the snow began on Wednesday. The report says the strike was short, and the report says the snow was heavy.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una decisión así dejó a muchos comerciantes sin ingresos.»

answer.text: Such

feedback.es: Such a + sustantivo califica la decisión ya mencionada y evita repetir toda la frase.

origin.text: The council closed the market for a week without any warning. ___ a decision left many traders without an income.

prompt.es: Une las dos ideas sin repetir palabras: usa such a… y respectively.

answer.text: The school closed the library during the exams. Such a decision upset pupils and teachers, who complained about the lack of space and of books respectively.
accepted: The school closed the library during the exams. Such a decision upset pupils and teachers, who complained about the lack of space and of books respectively.
The school closed its library during the exams. Such a measure upset pupils and teachers, who complained about the lack of space and of books respectively.
The school closed the library for the exams, and such a move upset pupils and teachers, who complained about the lack of space and the lack of books respectively.

feedback.es: Una referencia como such a decision resume el cierre y respectively empareja cada grupo con su queja en el mismo orden.

origin.text: Ideas: el colegio cerró la biblioteca durante los exámenes; los alumnos se quejaron de la falta de espacio y los profesores de la falta de libros. Escríbelo en dos frases sin repetir palabras, con una referencia que resuma el cierre y respectively.

prompt.es: ¿Qué opina la editora de las dos mitades del borrador?

choices.text: The first half is clearer, because it uses fewer references.
Both parts need the same correction for repeating one word.
The second half handles its references better than the first.
She sees nothing to improve in either part of the draft.

feedback.es: «The latter half is better than the former» significa que la segunda mitad (latter) es mejor que la primera (former).

origin.text: Dear Carlos, the draft reads well, but the same word, plan, opens six sentences on the second page. Replacing some of them with such a measure or this approach would help, although you should check that each one points clearly to the previous sentence. In this respect, the latter half of the draft is better than the former. Best wishes, Mia.

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo mismo se aplica a las entrevistas con los profesores.»

answer.text: applies

feedback.es: The same applies to + sustantivo extiende lo dicho a otro caso sin repetirlo.

origin.text: Only fifty pupils answered the survey. The same ___ to the interviews with teachers, which reached just six people.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En este sentido, los dos informes difieren mucho.»

answer.text: In this respect the two reports differ greatly
accepted: In this respect the two reports differ greatly
The two reports differ greatly in this respect

feedback.es: In this respect limita la comparación a un aspecto concreto.

title.es: Detectar los fallos de un borrador

es: Leer un borrador y localizar repeticiones, referencias ambiguas, saltos lógicos, frases irrelevantes y contradicciones, nombrando cada problema.

vocabulary.es: non sequitur, conclusión que no se deduce
antecedente (a lo que remite un pronombre)

teaching.en: A rough draft is often repetitive: the same noun opens every sentence, and the reader hears an echo instead of an argument.
teaching.es: Un borrador suele ser repetitivo: el mismo sustantivo abre cada frase, y el lector oye un eco en lugar de un argumento.
teaching.explanationEs: Repetitive describe un texto que insiste con las mismas palabras.
segments: A rough draft is often repetitive: the same noun opens every
sentence, and the reader hears an echo instead of an argument.
teaching.audioText: A rough draft is often repetitive: the same noun opens every sentence, and the reader hears an echo instead of an argument.

teaching.en: In the sentence Ana told Mia that she was late, the pronoun is ambiguous, since its antecedent could be either girl.
teaching.es: En la frase «Ana le dijo a Mia que ella llegaba tarde», el pronombre es ambiguo, pues su antecedente podría ser cualquiera de las dos.
teaching.explanationEs: El antecedente es la palabra a la que remite un pronombre.
segments: In the sentence Ana told Mia that she was late, the
pronoun is ambiguous, since its antecedent could be either girl.
teaching.audioText: In the sentence Ana told Mia that she was late, the pronoun is ambiguous, since its antecedent could be either girl.

teaching.en: A writer who jumps to a conclusion leaves a logical gap, so the reader stays unclear about the reasoning.
teaching.es: Un autor que saca conclusiones precipitadas deja un salto lógico, y el lector sigue sin tener claro el razonamiento.
teaching.explanationEs: Jumps to a conclusion = concluye sin pasos intermedios.
segments: A writer who jumps to a conclusion leaves a logical
gap, so the reader stays unclear about the reasoning.
teaching.audioText: A writer who jumps to a conclusion leaves a logical gap, so the reader stays unclear about the reasoning.

teaching.en: A paragraph on school buses should not go off on a tangent about holidays, because an irrelevant sentence weakens the point.
teaching.es: Un párrafo sobre autobuses escolares no debería irse por las ramas hablando de vacaciones, porque una frase irrelevante debilita la idea.
teaching.explanationEs: Irrelevant = no tiene que ver con el tema del párrafo.
segments: A paragraph on school buses should not go off on a
tangent about holidays, because an irrelevant sentence weakens the point.
teaching.audioText: A paragraph on school buses should not go off on a tangent about holidays, because an irrelevant sentence weakens the point.

teaching.en: When one sentence contradicts another, the paragraph collapses, and a non sequitur, which follows from nothing, does the same damage.
teaching.es: Cuando una frase contradice a otra, el párrafo se viene abajo, y un non sequitur, que no se deduce de nada, hace el mismo daño.
teaching.explanationEs: Contradicts lleva objeto directo: contradicts the first sentence, sin to.
segments: When one sentence contradicts another, the paragraph collapses, and a
non sequitur, which follows from nothing, does the same damage.
teaching.audioText: When one sentence contradicts another, the paragraph collapses, and a non sequitur, which follows from nothing, does the same damage.

teaching.en: Vague wording such as things or stuff leaves the reader unclear about the point, so replace it with the exact noun.
teaching.es: Una redacción vaga, con palabras como «cosas», deja al lector sin tener claro el punto, así que sustitúyela por el sustantivo exacto.
teaching.explanationEs: Vague wording = palabras demasiado generales; se opone a precise.
segments: Vague wording such as things or stuff leaves the reader unclear
about the point, so replace it with the exact noun.
teaching.audioText: Vague wording such as things or stuff leaves the reader unclear about the point, so replace it with the exact noun.

prompt.es: ¿Qué problema principal tiene este fragmento del borrador?

choices.text: It is repetitive: the same noun opens every sentence.
It is ambiguous: each pronoun could refer to two things.
It contradicts itself about the size of the town.

feedback.es: Las tres frases empiezan por «The town» y no aportan una progresión: el problema es la repetición.

origin.text: The town is small. The town has a river. The town has a market. The town has a school.

prompt.es: Completa: «Palabras como «cosas» son vagas: no dan nada concreto que imaginar.»

answer.text: vague

feedback.es: Vague describe una palabra demasiado general; la solución es sustituirla por el sustantivo exacto.

hint.es: Adjetivo que se opone a specific.

origin.text: Words such as things and stuff are ___, because they give readers nothing exact to picture. A precise noun is always better.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La segunda frase contradice directamente a la primera.»

answer.text: The second sentence directly contradicts the first one

feedback.es: Contradicts es transitivo: va seguido de the first one, sin preposición.

hint.es: Directly va justo antes del verbo contradicts.

prompt.es: Identifica el problema principal del párrafo.

choices.text: It is ambiguous: the pronouns could refer to two different things.
It contradicts itself about how many members the club has.
It jumps to a conclusion that the figures do not support.

prompt.es: Escribe un párrafo sobre una decisión y dos reescrituras concisas (230–290 palabras).

answer.text: Last year I decided to leave my hometown and study in another city. Admittedly, the choice was not easy, because my family lives there and I had never lived alone. Nevertheless, I wanted a course that my local college did not offer, so I got to the point and applied. At first I was homesick, and the flat was small and noisy. However, I soon found friends, and my classes were better than I expected. My parents were worried at first, but they supported me in the end. Looking back, I am glad that I trusted my own judgement, although I still miss my mother's cooking. Long version: Due to the fact that I wanted to save money, I made a decision to work at weekends. However, I soon found friends, and my classes were better than I expected. My parents were worried at first, but they supported me in the end. Looking back, I am glad that I trusted my own judgement, although I still miss my mother's cooking. Long version: Due to the fact that I wanted to save money, I made a decision to work at weekends. Concise version: Because I wanted to save money, I decided to work at weekends. Long version: In order to be able to concentrate, I turned off my phone at this point in time. Concise version: To concentrate, I turned off my phone.

Two years ago I decided to change schools, and it was the hardest choice of my life. Admittedly, I was afraid of leaving my friends, and my parents were not sure either. Nevertheless, the new school offered music lessons that my old school did not, so I made up my mind and moved. The first weeks were difficult, because nobody knew me and the timetable was confusing. Even so, I soon joined the choir, and I am happy with my decision today. My parents now say that the move changed my life, and my old friends often visit me. prompt.es: Redacta el artículo de opinión con revisión documentada (250–310 palabras).

answer.text: I will argue that the school should not ban phones at break, because a ban solves the wrong problem. First, pupils use their phones to talk to friends who are in other classes, and this contact is the only chance they have to do so. Second, a ban teaches pupils to hide their phones instead of using them well. Last term, for example, my class agreed on a simple rule and complaints fell by half. Admittedly, some pupils spend the whole break looking at a screen. Nevertheless, this is a problem of habits, not of phones, and, as mentioned above, a rule that pupils help to write is easier to respect. Some teachers take issue with this view, but a sensible alternative would be phone-free zones, which persuade without pushing anybody. I also believe that the school should trust us more, because trust is the best way to teach responsibility. In conclusion, the school should give us a say and trust us to use our phones well. Revision: I cut two repeated phrases and replaced due to the fact that with because.

In my opinion, the school should not take phones away at break, because a ban would hurt pupils who use them sensibly. First, many of us talk to friends from other classes, and this is often our only chance to do so. Second, a strict rule would teach us to hide our phones rather than to control them. Last year, for instance, our class made its own rule, and arguments about phones almost disappeared. It is true that some pupils stare at a screen for the whole break. Even so, this is a question of habits, and, as noted above, rules that pupils help to write are easier to respect. A reasonable alternative would be quiet zones, where phones are allowed only for messages. Some teachers take issue with this view, but I think it is fair to ask them for trust. In short, pupils deserve a say in this decision, and the magazine should keep asking for it. Revision: I trimmed two long sentences and removed a repeated example.

feedback.es: En la nota, «the former argument is clearer than the latter» indica que el argumento citado antes es más claro y el citado después aún necesita un ejemplo.

origin.audio: Dear Sara, your piece is persuasive, and the ending is strong. Two small things: the former argument is clearer than the latter, which needs an example, and the phrase due to the fact that appears twice, so please tighten it up. As mentioned above, I would keep the concession, because it makes you sound fair. Best wishes, Carlos.
